records.what_adobe_says: A client that already licenses Coworker can ask its marketing questions (audiences, journeys, campaign performance, Workfront projects) from inside the assistant its staff already use. In ChatGPT, the ChatGPT administrator approves Adobe CX Enterprise Coworker, then each person installs it from the Plugins catalog. In Claude, the Claude administrator approves it, then each person finds it under Customize, Connectors, connects it and signs in with their Adobe login. People see only what their Adobe permissions already allow; answers are read-only and nothing in the client's customer data is changed. There is no extra charge: it is part of the Coworker license and uses the same AI credits. First the client needs Coworker, Adobe Experience Platform and at least one of Real-Time CDP, Journey Optimizer or Customer Journey Analytics. Real limits: not everything in Coworker's own screen works in an assistant, Firefly image generation does not work through Claude, and only the assistants on Adobe's list can be connected.

wrong_or_unsupported_in_research: It names only ChatGPT and Claude. Adobe's page lists seven assistants, each with its own setup: Microsoft 365 Copilot, ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini Enterprise, Amazon Quick, IBM watsonx Orchestrate and Databricks.

Its third source, a claude.com marketplace page whose address ends in 'adobe-marketing-agent', is not an Adobe site and does not count as evidence. It was not opened. The name in that address is not the name Adobe's page tells people to look for in Claude, which is 'Adobe CX Enterprise Coworker'.
'Validate a use case against the correct sandbox/data view' is the research's own idea of partner work. Adobe's page does not mention sandboxes or data views.

'Sign in with a permitted Adobe identity': Adobe writes the Adobe sign-in step for Claude (and for Amazon Quick, IBM and Databricks). The ChatGPT steps on the page end at 'Install plugin' and do not spell out a sign-in step; only the troubleshooting section says to sign in again with Adobe credentials.

It labels the ChatGPT and Claude route as an 'MCP connector'. Adobe's page uses the words 'plugin' (ChatGPT) and 'Connectors' (Claude) and only uses the term MCP for Amazon Quick, IBM watsonx Orchestrate and Databricks.
'Feature availability varies by host, including Firefly image generation' is vaguer than Adobe: the one stated difference is that Firefly image generation is not available through Claude.

Second reader: Adobe's news release is not consistent about IBM (its summary says IBM is "to follow", its first paragraph says IBM watsonx Orchestrate is available now). This does not affect ChatGPT or Claude.
Second reader: IBM watsonx Orchestrate and Databricks need one more step that ChatGPT and Claude do not: the client confirms sign-in settings with its Adobe representative before setup.
records.release_label: none stated for ChatGPT or Claude. Adobe's news release of November 4, 2026 says "now available within leading AI platforms ChatGPT (as a plugin), Claude, Databricks Genie, Gemini for business, IBM watsonx Orchestrate and Microsoft Copilot" and "with availability in Amazon Quick and Snowflake expected soon". The same release's opening summary says "with Amazon Web Services (AWS), IBM and Snowflake to follow", so the release contradicts itself on IBM; Adobe's setup page (also dated November 4) gives full steps for IBM watsonx Orchestrate and Amazon Quick and does not mention Snowflake. None of this touches ChatGPT or Claude, which both the release and the setup page treat as available. The words "private offer" on the page are about Google's purchase step for Gemini, and "limited introductory period" is about the price in AI credits; neither is a release label.

records.assistant: both. Adobe names ChatGPT and Claude, each with its own ready-made listing for Customer Journey Analytics. For Claude, Adobe's guide speaks of "the Claude standalone application" and its guide list of "the Claude web app". records.what_adobe_says: A client's analysts can ask Customer Journey Analytics questions in plain language inside ChatGPT or Claude and get reports back from their own data views. Adobe publishes it ready-made in both: in ChatGPT a person opens Plugins, searches for CJA and installs it; in Claude a person opens Customize, Connectors, searches for Customer Journey Analytics and connects it. Each person signs in with their Adobe login. With the read-only permission they can look things up and run reports; with the full permission they can also create or change segments, calculated metrics, date ranges, Workspace projects and audiences, as long as their normal Customer Journey Analytics permissions allow it too. It costs nothing extra; the reports count toward the client's monthly report allowance. First an Adobe administrator must add one of the two permissions to the person's product profile, and ChatGPT users need a Plus or Pro subscription. Real limits: a report returns at most 100 rows per request, reports cannot be scheduled, and administration (such as editing data views) cannot be done this way.

other_leads: Coworker reaches five more assistants than the research names. Adobe's Coworker page gives setup steps for Microsoft 365 Copilot, Gemini Enterprise, Amazon Quick, IBM watsonx Orchestrate and Databricks Genie One as well as ChatGPT and Claude (https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/coworker/content/ai-platforms).

Snowflake: Adobe's news release says availability in 'Amazon Quick and Snowflake' is 'expected soon'. Snowflake is not on Adobe's setup page, so under the step 86 rule it is left out. Amazon Quick is on the setup page with full steps, even though the release of the same day calls it 'expected soon' (https://news.adobe.com/news/2026/11/adobe-integrates-agentic-cx-enterprise-coworker-into-ai-platforms).

Marketing Campaign Analytics (in the tool as 'mmm'): Adobe says 'Currently, the Marketing Campaign Analytics MCP server is only available through Adobe CX Enterprise Coworker.' So it has no direct ChatGPT or Claude route of its own; it is reached through Coworker (https://developer.adobe.com/analytics-mcp/docs/).

Adobe Analytics and Customer Journey Analytics also have Adobe setup guides for Cursor and Microsoft Copilot Studio, and a route for the client's own programs with no assistant at all; Gemini is 'CLI-only support; guide forthcoming', marked 'Coming soon' (https://developer.adobe.com/analytics-mcp/docs/guides/).

A different kind of ChatGPT work, not a connection to an Adobe product's data: Adobe documents how a client's own ChatGPT App can send usage data to Adobe Experience Platform and show personalized content ('Collect analytics and apply personalization in ChatGPT Apps'). Adobe calls it 'a reference implementation' (https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/experience-platform/collection/use-cases/mcp/chatgpt).

The tool already has a service for record 0: 'Coworker set up in an AI platform' (8, 16 or 32 hours) points at the same Adobe page, and the 'Approved Coworker connection or plugin' service already cites the same news release. A ChatGPT or Claude outside system for Coworker can reuse that service instead of adding a new one.

Adobe's own caution, worth keeping as a real limit: 'Connecting MCP clients or servers to Adobe products is a customer-elected configuration. Customers are responsible for evaluating the security and suitability of any MCP integration.' and whether the assistant's maker trains on the data 'depends on your agreement with the LLM provider, not Adobe' (https://developer.adobe.com/analytics-mcp/docs/ and .../support/faq).

Adobe Analytics and Customer Journey Analytics connected at the same time can confuse the assistant: Adobe's fix is to connect only the one needed for the session (https://developer.adobe.com/analytics-mcp/docs/support/troubleshooting).

second_reader.method: All 55 first-check quotes (48 in the three records plus the 7 platform quotes on the Coworker page; shared quotes counted each time they appear) were matched word for word against the saved files with the project matcher, then all 14 pages were fetched again with curl (default headers, one request a second), found to be the same size, and matched again. Each page was read in full around the quotes and searched for beta, preview, private, early access, coming soon, forthcoming, roadmap, pilot and experimental. 19 quotes were added by the second reader and matched the same way. No verdict changed.
